<!-- Generated by esquadro docs from the blueprint's manifest: do not edit. -->

The project's CI on GitHub Actions, for any kind of app: go vet, the tests (the runner has Docker, for testcontainers), the build, and a check that the generated code is what the model generates (esquadro gen -check, with the esquadro version of the lockfile). With docker, on tags v*, it builds the image and publishes it to GitHub's container registry (ghcr.io/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo>). It runs as little as it can, to save Actions minutes: pushes to the long-lived branches only (pull requests cover the others), no runs for draft pull requests, older runs cancelled.

```esquadro
blueprint github_actions
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [app](../app/): the app must use them too.
- **Works with** [docker](../docker/) when the app uses them.

## Slots

Other blueprints add code at these points (see [Writing a blueprint](/esquadro/writing-blueprints/#slots)).

| Slot | |
|---|---|
| `github_actions.branches` | Branches whose pushes run the CI, as items of a YAML list, e.g. main, develop, "release/**"; main when nobody contributes. |
| `github_actions.test.steps` | Steps run first in the test job, as YAML indented by six spaces, e.g. a check of the pull request's branch name. |
| `github_actions.jobs` | Jobs of the CI workflow, as YAML indented by two spaces. Each job is billed by the minute, rounded up: prefer a step of the test job. |
| `github_actions.image.steps` | Steps run after the image is published, in the image job, as YAML indented by six spaces, e.g. a deploy. |
